title: Energy (E&P)
objectives: Answer out loud: Why NAV instead of a perpetuity DCF?

steps.body: Exploration & production companies find and extract oil and gas. Value depends on reserves and commodity prices.
Metrics: EV/EBITDAX, NAV of reserves, EV/production ($ per flowing barrel), EV/reserves.

blocks.title: Why EBITDAX instead of EBITDA?
blocks.body:
Companies account for exploration differently. Under successful efforts, failed exploration costs (dry holes) are expensed; under full cost, they're capitalized. Adding back exploration expense makes companies using different methods comparable.

**Interview answer:** "Exploration accounting differs between successful efforts and full cost, so we add exploration back to compare them."

blocks.prompt: Why do analysts use EBITDAX for E&P companies?

options.text: Exploration accounting differs (successful efforts vs. full cost), so adding it back makes companies comparable
Because E&P companies have no depreciation

blocks.explanation: Successful-efforts companies expense dry holes; full-cost companies capitalize them. Adding back exploration expense levels the playing field.

blocks.title: How does an NAV model work?
blocks.teaser: Project production from each reserve category until depletion, apply a commodity price deck, subtract costs and taxes, and discount (often at 10% — P…
blocks.body: Project production from each reserve category until depletion, apply a commodity price deck, subtract costs and taxes, and discount (often at 10% — PV-10). Sum the reserves, subtract net debt. Risk probable and possible reserves at lower percentages.

blocks.title: Why isn't a standard DCF terminal value used?
blocks.body: Reserves are finite and deplete. An NAV model projects to depletion instead of assuming cash flows forever.

blocks.title: How do hedges affect value?
blocks.teaser: Hedging locks in prices for part of production, reducing exposure to commodity swings.
blocks.body: Hedging locks in prices for part of production, reducing exposure to commodity swings. Model hedged volumes at hedge prices and the rest at the price deck.
